board: New Jersey State Board of Accountancy (Division of Consumer Affairs)

cycle.label: Triennial period
cycle.note: One triennial period for everyone (currently Jan 1, 2024 – Dec 31, 2026); licenses renew by December 31 at the end of it.

requirements.label: Technical subjects
requirements.note: At least 60 of the 120 in accounting, auditing, business law, computer science, economics, finance, MAS, math/statistics, SEC practice, taxation or professional ethics.

requirements.label: Accounting & auditing (public practice)
requirements.note: 24 hours in accounting or auditing (review and compilation count) if you're in the practice of public accountancy.

requirements.label: New Jersey Law & Ethics
requirements.note: The Board-approved 4-hour New Jersey Law & Ethics course, taken in person or by live webinar from an approved provider. We count courses with "New Jersey" (or "NJ") and "ethics" in the title.

newLicensee.note: First renewal after licensure: the 120 / 20-per-year / technical / A&A requirements don't apply. The 4-hour New Jersey Law & Ethics course still does.

licenseDateHint: New Jersey licenses renew by December 31 at the end of each triennial period (currently 12/31/2026).
issueDateHint: If you were licensed during this triennial period, only the NJ Law & Ethics course is due at your first renewal.
toVerify: Technical list is from N.J.A.C. 13:29-6.3 as quoted by NASBA ('Professional Ethics' — both ethics fields treated as technical). Specialized Knowledge isn't listed, so it's treated as non-technical (conservative).
New licensees: the ethics course is kept for the first renewal ('All applicants shall complete four credits…'), everything else waived.
The in-person/webinar requirement for the NJ ethics course isn't checked against the course's delivery format.
